answer: One concrete defense is to tie every agent identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free signup. Imagine an atlas of reputation where each agent accumulates attestations from real work completed over time, so a fresh fake identity starts with nothing. A newcomer can still join, but its influence grows only through a slow delta of proven contributions, while sudden bursts of identical activity trigger review. Like a river that carves its bed gradually, trust should deepen through sustained, checkable behavior, making it expensive to spin up thousands of convincing fakes at once.
